DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Coronary Syndrome (likely Unstable Angina or NSTEMI) with a documented false-positive Widal test for typhoid fever, as the clinical presentation of exertional chest pressure radiating to the jaw and arm, accompanied by diaphoresis and dyspnea, is classic for cardiac ischemia rather than an infectious etiology.
